proposal: Pay market makers a 2 basis point rebate and charge takers 3

compiled.hypothesis: Paying makers and charging takers will encourage liquidity provision and tighten spreads.
compiled.restated: Set maker_fee_bps to -2 (a 2 bps rebate to makers) and taker_fee_bps to 3.

memo.caveats: Based on only 3 paired seeds in scenario normal with AI makers (Muse Spark and Muse Spark Open) and GLFT optimal maker. Institutional shortfall (-0.153, SE 0.512), Top-5 depth (-0.769 lots, SE 1.571), volatility (-0.128 bps, SE 0.109) and worst drawdown (0.0%, SE 0.033) are all smaller than about two standard errors and are not established. Established effects remain uncertain due to small n.
memo.summary: Retail all-in cost rose by +2.087 bps (SE 0.476, 3/3 up) from 4.726 to 6.813 bps. Quoted spread narrowed by -1.863 cents (SE 0.806, 0/3 up) from 8.471 to 6.608 cents, but did not translate to lower all-in cost. Mispricing vs fair value rose by +0.588 bps (SE 0.187, 3/3 up) from 26.794 to 27.383 bps. Institutional shortfall, depth, volatility and drawdown changes were smaller than about two SEs and are not established.
memo.who_gains: Market makers, whose P&L rose by +562.756 per epoch (SE 81.307, 3/3 up) from 834.556 to 1397.311, and the exchange, whose fee revenue rose by +9692.8 (SE 198.291, 3/3 up) from 0.0 to 9692.8.
memo.who_pays: Retail investors, whose all-in cost rose as measured above despite narrower quoted spreads, and who face higher measured mispricing; no clear change established for institutional shortfall.

proposal: Add a 10 basis point financial transaction tax

compiled.hypothesis: Trading activity will decrease as higher costs discourage transactions.
compiled.restated: Impose a 10 basis point financial transaction tax paid by both sides.

memo.caveats: Paired comparison vs today's rules on only 3 seeds in normal scenario with AI (Muse Spark and Muse Spark Open) and GLFT optimal makers; do not generalize beyond this wind tunnel. Institutional shortfall change +4.246 bps (SE 3.463, 2 of 3 up) and worst drawdown change +0.045% (SE 0.026) are smaller than ~2 SE and therefore not established. Even established effects have wide uncertainty from n=3.
memo.summary: Retail all-in cost rose from 4.14 to 16.503 bps, change +12.362 bps (SE 0.633, 3 of 3 up), with quoted spread up +4.048 cents (SE 1.486) and Top-5 depth down -6.78 lots (SE 0.35). Volatility per step rose +0.518 bps (SE 0.121) while mispricing vs fair value eased only -0.433 bps (SE 0.171); institutional shortfall +4.246 bps (SE 3.463) and worst drawdown +0.045% (SE 0.026) are not established. Market makers' P&L fell -1830.089 per epoch (SE 216.607) from 688.352 to -1141.737 while tax revenue rose +193658.733 (SE 4119.992) from 0.
memo.who_gains: The tax recipient gains revenue, measured at 193658.733 (SE 4119.992); no investor group shows an established gain except a small -0.433 bps (SE 0.171) reduction in mispricing.
memo.who_pays: Retail traders pay higher all-in cost and face wider spreads, thinner depth and higher volatility; market makers pay via sharply lower P&L turning to loss; institutional extra cost is not established in these 3 seeds.

proposal: Ban short selling during a crash

compiled.hypothesis: Banning non-market-maker short sales during a crash will reduce downward price pressure and stabilize prices.
compiled.restated: Ban all non-market-maker short sales during a crash.

memo.caveats: Only 3 paired seeds in crash scenario with AI (Muse Spark and Muse Spark Open) and GLFT makers; all standard errors are large, so material effects in either direction cannot be ruled out; results do not generalize beyond crash conditions tested.
memo.summary: In a crash with 3 paired seeds, banning short sales showed no established changes: retail cost changed -0.025 bps (SE 0.284, 2 up) and institutional shortfall -8.223 bps (SE 10.584, 1 up), both well under ~2 SE. Mispricing -7.089 bps (SE 5.185, 0 up), volatility -0.385 bps (SE 0.47), spread -0.188 cents (SE 0.271), depth -0.505 lots (SE 0.606) and worst drawdown -0.139% (SE 0.219) are also not established. Maker P&L rose +559.648 per epoch (SE 294.629, 3 up) but at ~1.9 SE remains below the threshold for an established effect.
memo.who_gains: No investor group is shown to gain: apparent improvements in retail cost, institutional shortfall, and mispricing are not established given SEs.
memo.who_pays: No group is shown to pay: there is no established worsening of costs, depth, volatility or drawdown, and the higher maker P&L is not established.

proposal: Route retail orders to a batch auction instead of the order book

compiled.hypothesis: Retail fills will move off-book into auctions, reducing lit-book retail interaction.
compiled.restated: Route all retail orders to a periodic batch auction instead of the lit order book.

memo.caveats: Only 3 paired seeds in the normal scenario with AI (Muse Spark and Muse Spark Open) and GLFT market makers; uncertainty is large and results may not generalize to other regimes or live behavior. Non-established differences should not be treated as zero or as proof of no effect.
memo.summary: Routing retail orders to a batch auction cut retail all-in cost from 4.257 bps to 1.859 bps (change -2.398 bps, SE 0.53, 0 of 3 seeds up), larger than about two standard errors and therefore established in this test. Institutional implementation shortfall (+0.151 bps, SE 0.811), quoted spread (+0.656 cents, SE 1.237), top-5 depth, mispricing, volatility and drawdown differences were all smaller than about two standard errors and are not established. Market makers' P&L change of -22.556 per epoch (SE 187.444, 2 of 3 seeds up) is also not established, so no offsetting transfer is demonstrated.
memo.who_gains: Retail investors, via lower measured retail all-in cost on all 3 paired seeds.
memo.who_pays: No payer is established in this test: differences for institutional shortfall, spread, depth, mispricing, volatility, drawdown, and market-maker P&L are all below about two standard errors.

proposal: Halt trading for a minute if the price moves 1%

compiled.hypothesis: Halting trading after a 1% move will dampen volatility and improve stability in a crash.
compiled.restated: Halt trading for 50 steps if the price moves 1% within 100 steps.

memo.caveats: Based on only 3 paired seeds in crash scenario with AI (Muse Spark and Muse Spark Open) and GLFT makers, so uncertainty is large. Institutional shortfall rose in 3/3 seeds but at 1.88 SEs is below the ~2 SE threshold and is not established; same for retail cost, spread, worst drawdown, and maker P&L. Conclusions apply only to this 1% halt calibration, not other thresholds or normal markets.
memo.summary: In a crash with 3 paired seeds, the 1% one-minute halt reduced Top-5 depth by 4.569 lots (SE 0.899, 0/3 up) from 42.355 to 37.786, increased mispricing vs fair value by 31.326 bps (SE 12.754, 3/3 up) from 42.186 to 73.512, and increased volatility per step by 1.845 bps (SE 0.232, 3/3 up) from 4.757 to 6.602. Changes in retail cost -0.083 bps (SE 0.234), institutional shortfall +23.904 bps (SE 12.708), quoted spread +0.309 cents (SE 0.509), worst drawdown +1.475% (SE 0.832), and maker P&L +799.426 per epoch (SE 791.689) are all smaller than about two SEs and are not established.
memo.who_gains: No group shows an established gain; market makers' P&L change of +799.426 per epoch (SE 791.689, 2/3 up) is not established.
memo.who_pays: Investors needing immediacy pay via established thinner Top-5 depth and face established higher mispricing and volatility; harm to retail trading cost, institutional shortfall, and worst drawdown is directionally adverse but not established.

proposal: Make every trader wear a hat

compiled.decline_reason: No lever controls trader attire; levers only cover tick size, fees, resting time, circuit breaker, transaction tax, short-sale ban, and retail routing.
compiled.restated: The proposal requires every trader to wear a hat.
